default_configuration.description: The build configuration to fall back on when neither `--configuration` nor a persisted selection names one: a tag declared on rules. When rules carry tags and this names none of them, the first declared tag is used and a warning is logged.

tracker.description: The [tracker] section: background polling of files.

documentation.description: The [documentation] section: how documentation comments are read.

document_symbols.description: The [document_symbols] section: what the outline lists.

semantic_tokens.description: The [semantic_tokens] section: what the semantic tokens hold and the names they are sent by.

references.description: The [references] section: what find references answers.

rules.description: File-pattern rules that adjust compilation flags ([[rules]] in clice.toml).

cache_dir.description: Directory for the unified on-disk cache (PCH, PCM and index artifacts). Empty defaults to `${workspace}/.clice`, which keeps itself out of version control and backups via generated .gitignore and CACHEDIR.TAG markers (a `.clice/config.toml` stays visible to Git; backup tools honoring CACHEDIR.TAG skip the whole directory); an explicitly configured directory is never marked. The resolved path is printed at startup.

logging_dir.description: Directory for log files; empty derives `${cache_dir}/logs`. Each server session logs into its own timestamped subdirectory.

enable_indexing.description: Build the background index that serves cross-TU features (find references, workspace symbols, ...).

standard_library_instantiations.description: Index what the standard library's own template instantiations and macros resolve inside the library — the comparator `std::sort` calls, the destructor `std::vector` runs — so references and the call hierarchy reach those places. Off by default: they are library internals, and walking them costs indexing time and space. Applies to the units indexed after a change.

skip_header_bodies.description: Skip the bodies of the functions in the headers an open file includes at its top, as clangd does, but those of templates forwarding their arguments (`make_unique`) and of `constexpr` and `auto` functions, which clang always parses. The file opens and rebuilds after an edit several times faster and holds less memory; the price is the errors and warnings inside those bodies, a header template's instantiated from the file among them, and whether a declaration is unused, which show only when the background index has compiled the file as it is saved. The background index and every command but `clice inspect` still compile the bodies.

readonly.description: Read-only serving for open files: "off" targets a full AST for every open file — builds are pulled by the first request that needs them, with the index answering in the meantime; "on" never builds a PCH — reads serve from the index alone (a cold file jumps the indexing queue), while completion and signature help still compile on demand without a preamble; "auto" starts every file as "on", switches it to "off" at the first edit intent (edit, completion, signature help, context switch), and falls back to "off" for a file the index cannot serve. Feature routing always answers from the best source currently available.

idle_timeout_ms.description: Idle delay in milliseconds before background indexing starts.

test_hooks.description: Enable the clice/internal test hooks used by the test harness.

stateful_worker_count.description: Number of stateful workers — they hold ASTs in memory and serve queries (hover, semantic tokens, ...); `0` is invalid and falls back to the default.

stateless_worker_count.description: Number of stateless workers started — they handle ephemeral tasks (PCH/PCM builds, completion, signature help, background indexing) — and the most that background indexing keeps busy at once; defaults to half the machine's physical cores, at least 2. `0` is invalid and falls back to that default.

min_stateless_worker_count.description: Lower bound for dynamic stateless-worker scaling; `0` is invalid and falls back to the default.

max_stateless_worker_count.description: Upper bound for dynamic stateless-worker scaling, which only interactive work that finds every worker busy reaches; `0` means the machine's physical cores, which is also the default.

workspace_poll_seconds.description: Longest interval in seconds between two background looks at a workspace file: the interval doubles at every look that finds the file unchanged, up to this. 0 disables background polling, compilation databases included.

clang_tidy.description: Run clang-tidy on open files and offer its fixes, with the checks the nearest `.clang-tidy` configures (a small default set without one). Checks too slow for an editor, and those unreliable on code being edited, are left out; files `clice lint` does not check get none. `NOLINT` comments also silence compiler warnings only while this runs.

suppress.description: Diagnostics open files do not show, by their code: a compiler warning's option (`-Wunused-variable`), clang's name for any other diagnostic (`err_undeclared_var_use`), a clang-tidy check, or one of clice's own warnings (`toolchain-query-failed`). For code clang gets wrong: everything else works on the file as before, and `clice lint` still reports them.

format.description: How documentation comments are read, wherever they show (hover, completion, signature help, `clice query`): "doxygen" reads Doxygen's commands (`@brief`, `@param`, `@return`, ...) and the Markdown Doxygen allows, along with the GTK-Doc and kernel-doc conventions; "plain" shows a comment as written.

inherit.description: An overriding method without a documentation comment shows the one of the method it overrides.

show_aka.description: Show what a type alias stands for, e.g. `size_type` is `unsigned long`.

max_members.description: Maximum number of members the definition of a hovered class or enum lists: data members and member types, or enumerators; member functions are left out. `0` shows the declaration alone.

layout.description: Show how the compiler lays out a class or a field wherever it is hovered: size, alignment, a field's offset, and the padding.

macros.description: List the `#define`s the file writes; an include guard's never lists.

locals.description: List what a function's body declares: its variables, types and lambdas, under the function.

types.description: Maximum length in characters of a deduced type or of deduced template arguments; `0` means no limit. The template arguments that do not fit become `…`, e.g. `tuple<int, string, …>`; a type whose outermost name does not fit is not shown.

default_arguments.description: Maximum length in characters of the omitted default arguments; `0` means no limit. One too long becomes `…`, and the list is cut with `…` where it no longer fits.

block_end.description: Maximum length in characters of a block end or namespace end label, cut with `…` past it; `0` means no limit.

endif.description: Maximum length in characters of an `#endif` condition, cut with `…` past it; `0` means no limit.

enabled.description: Master switch: `false` disables all inlay hints.

parameters.description: Parameter name hints at call sites, e.g. `draw(width: 800, height: 600)`.

mutable_references.description: `&` marking an argument passed by mutable reference, e.g. `mutate(&value: v)`.

prefixed_names.description: Parameter name hints for an argument named like the parameter without its one-letter prefix, e.g. `param` passed to `aParam`.

single_letter_names.description: Parameter name hints for a function taking one parameter whose name is a single letter, e.g. `push_back(x: 1)`.

deduced_types.description: Deduced type hints for `auto` variables, structured bindings, init-captures and `auto` parameters, the type a `decltype` names, and deduced return types.

spelled_types.description: Deduced type hints for a variable whose initializer already names its type, e.g. `static_cast<long>(x)`, `Widget{1, 2}` or `std::make_unique<Widget>()`.

deduced_template_arguments.description: The template arguments class template argument deduction found, e.g. `<int, double>` after `pair` in `std::pair pair(1, 2.5)`.

designators.description: Field designator hints in aggregate initialization, e.g. `.x=` and `.y=` in `Point{1, 2}`.

array_indices.description: Array index designator hints in aggregate initialization, e.g. `[0]=` and `[1]=` in `int pair[2] = {1, 2}`.

block_end.description: `// name` after the closing brace of a function, type or control flow block, linking to its start.

namespace_end.description: `// namespace name` after the closing brace of a namespace, linking to its start.

endif.description: `// condition` after an `#endif`, the condition of the `#if` it closes, linking to it.

default_arguments.description: The default arguments a call omitted.

min_block_lines.description: The height in lines, both ends included, from which a block, namespace or conditional gets a hint at its end.

max_length.description: The [inlay_hints.max_length] table: how long each kind of hint may grow.

lexical.description: Send the tokens an editor's own syntax highlighting colors as well: keywords, literals, comments, operators, preprocessor directives. When off, only what syntax cannot tell is sent: names by what they name, overloaded and declarator operators, template brackets, format specifiers, and the tokens of preprocessor-inactive code, kindless.

kinds.description: The names a client or theme expects for clice's token kinds, as `field = "property"`; an empty name drops the kind, whose tokens are then not sent, and kinds given one name merge. Read when the server starts.

modifiers.description: The names a client or theme expects for clice's token modifiers; an empty name drops the modifier, and modifiers given one name merge. Read when the server starts.

arguments.description: What completing a call or a template inserts after the name: "placeholders" its parentheses or angle brackets with a placeholder per parameter, "delimiters" the empty parentheses or brackets with the cursor between them, "none" the name alone. It applies to functions, function-like macros, variables holding a lambda and class, alias and variable templates; an overload set listed as one item takes the delimiters. Nothing is added where the arguments are written already or the name is not called, as when taking a function's address. Clients without snippet support get the parentheses of a call alone.

bundle_overloads.description: Collapse an overload set into a single completion item.

statement_snippets.description: Complete statements such as `if` and `for` as snippets with placeholders for their parts; otherwise only the keyword is inserted. Ignored for clients without snippet support.

dot_to_arrow.description: After `.` on a pointer, list the members `->` reaches and turn the `.` into `->` when one is chosen.

all_scopes.description: Where an unqualified name is being typed, also offer the project's names of other namespaces it matches, inserting the qualifier they need; one in several namespaces is offered once per namespace. Names the file reaches already are offered as they are; for the others see `insert_includes` and `insert_imports`. Needs the index for names the file does not reach.

insert_includes.description: With `all_scopes`, also offer names declared, and macros defined, in headers the file does not include yet, adding the `#include` of the header that holds them.

insert_imports.description: With `all_scopes`, also offer names exported by modules the file does not import yet, adding the `import`.

limit.description: Maximum number of completion items, the best ranked; `0` means no limit. A list cut short is marked incomplete, so the editor asks again as you type.

documentation.description: Show the called function's documentation comment.

limit.description: Maximum number of locations a references request answers with; `0` means no limit. A reply cut short keeps the locations in the file it is asked from before any other. `clice query references` lists every one.

patterns.description: Glob patterns selecting the files this rule applies to. A relative pattern is anchored at this configuration file's directory (`..` segments allowed), or at the workspace root for a rule passed through initializationOptions; an absolute pattern or one starting with `**` matches the file's absolute path. `*` matches within a path segment, `?` a single character, `**` any number of segments, `{a,b}` alternatives, `[0-9]` a character range, `[!...]` a negated range. Omitted means every file.

configuration.description: Build configuration tag. A tagged rule applies only while that configuration is active; an untagged rule always applies. The distinct tags form the configuration menu; `--configuration`, the persisted selection and `default_configuration` pick the active one, in that order.

compile_commands.description: Compilation databases, in priority order: a compile_commands.json or a directory containing one, relative to this configuration file (to the workspace root for a rule passed through initializationOptions). All of them load, and every entry applies to its own file whatever the patterns say; the patterns and the order decide which entry a file present in several databases gets by default. A rule without patterns names the workspace's databases. When no rule declares a source, every compile_commands.json in the workspace root and its immediate subdirectories loads, and so do the ones in the directories above a file when it is opened.

resolve_symlinks.description: Whether builds are told apart by the real paths this rule's `compile_commands` resolve to, through symlinks and Windows junctions, rather than by the configuration's name: for a build system that selects a build by pointing a link at its directory. Each real path keeps an index of its own, and when the link is pointed elsewhere the server switches to that build's index, which still holds what an earlier session indexed there. A configuration whose rules differ from this configuration's only in naming exactly those databases directly shares its index. The index of a build no longer used stays in the cache directory until deleted.

default_command.description: The compile command for matching files without a database entry, without the source file: a string tokenized like a shell command line, or an argv array. It runs from the directory of the configuration file it was read from (the workspace root for a rule passed through initializationOptions), and the matching source files on disk join the background index (unless the rule turns `index` off) — enumerated at startup and again on every workspace poll, so a file created later compiles when opened and joins the index within a poll period. A file clang has no language for (an Arduino `.ino`, an extensionless tool) is a source only when the command forces a language (`-x c++`) and a pattern names its suffix (`*.ino`) or the file itself. Omitted means none.

append.description: Compilation flags appended for matching files, e.g. `["-std=c++20", "-DNDEBUG"]`.

remove.description: Compilation flags removed for matching files, e.g. `["-Wall"]`. A flag with a value removes that value (`-DDEBUG`), the next element being a separate value as on a command line; one with `*` for its value (`-I*`, `["-include", "*"]`), or without one at the end of the list (`["-include"]`), removes every value; a `*` right after a flag's name removes every flag of its kind spelled with that prefix (`-W*` takes `-Wall` and `-Wextra` too).

query_toolchain.description: Whether clice runs the compiler of matching files' commands to ask how it compiles them: its target, standard library and system headers, predefined macros and default language standard. `false` runs no compiler: clice's own clang reads the command as written, with clang's defaults for the compiler's name. Any matching rule saying `false` wins.

index.description: Whether matching translation units join the background index. `false` keeps them out; they still compile when opened and still host the headers they include. Any matching rule saying `false` wins.

lint.description: Whether `clice lint` checks matching files. `false` keeps them out: their findings are dropped and a translation unit they head is not parsed, unless `--index` needs it for the index. Files outside the workspace are never checked. Any matching rule saying `false` wins.

format.description: Whether `clice format` formats matching files. `false` keeps them out. Files outside the workspace are never formatted. Any matching rule saying `false` wins.
